# Product and merchant markup

Google said shopping is where structured data's precision matters most: LLM extraction gets complex pricing such as sale prices wrong, and markup stops its systems from picking up prices of related products (said at the event, not in Google's docs). In 2025 Google added structured data support for merchant loyalty programs and shipping policies, set at organisation level with product-level details. On stage, validity dates for sale prices were presented as new support added in the months before the event, so merchants need not rush to remove a sale price when a sale ends; Google's documentation updates log calls the July 2026 change a clarification, a Sale duration section explaining validFrom with validThrough or priceValidUntil, aligned with Merchant Center's sale_price_effective_date. Google's guide to pausing an online business recommends staying online and updating Product markup to show current availability. Day 3 brought the promised shopping detail: product rich results and Google Images product annotations come from product structured data without Merchant Center, while the Shopping tab needs a Merchant Center feed; product snippets draw on both, Google's documentation recommends feed and markup together for the widest eligibility, and Merchant Center can use the markup to fix mismatched feed data. Basic product markup has product data (name, description, brand, images) and offer data (URL, condition, availability, price), and an offer can reference shipping and return policies defined once under Organization through @id, as Google's merchant listing documentation recommends. Google Shopping said most of its new conversational attributes can also be read from schema.org markup, and schema.org added properties such as specification and valueGroup in September 2026, but Google's documentation did not cover this markup on 3 October 2026, so the feed is the documented route. Google's merchant listing documentation lists the product name as a required property and, unlike product snippets, requires a price greater than zero for merchant listing experiences; a Day 1 community demo's test page was flagged for an empty name and a price of zero.

Based on: `D2-C459`, `D2-C473`, `D2-C505`, `D2-C506`, `D2-C507`, `D2-C012`, `D2-C509`, `D3-C343`, `D3-C345`, `D3-C346`, `D3-C354`, `D3-C344`, `D3-C350`, `D3-C382`, `D3-C383`, `D3-C384`, `D3-C380`, `D3-C399`, `D3-C400`, `D3-C381`, `D1-C507`, `D1-C502`.

## What to do

- Give sale prices validity dates in Product markup and keep them aligned with the Merchant Center feed.
- On pages with related-product or recently viewed carousels, make the Product markup describe only the main item and its price.
- Define loyalty programs and shipping policies at organisation level and add product-level details where needed.
- When pausing sales, keep product pages online and show current availability on the page and in the markup.
- Keep price, availability, brand and GTIN identical in feed and markup, and reference shipping and return policies from each Offer by @id.
- Give every product a name and a price above zero in its markup; a zero price fails merchant listing experiences.

## What Google's documentation says

- **[Docs]** Google's merchant listing documentation lists the product name as a required property and, unlike product snippets, requires a price greater than zero for merchant listing experiences.
  <br><sub>`D1-C507` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 1, Lightning session A: Automation and AI · is the documentation · [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing) · Used by `DEV-SDA-08`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's guide to temporarily pausing an online business recommends that a shop expecting to sell again within weeks or months stays online with limited functionality, such as a disabled cart, and updates its Product structured data to show current availability.
  <br><sub>`D2-C012` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Welcome to indexing day! · is the documentation · [Temporarily pause or disable a website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/pause-online-business) · Used by `DEV-ERR-04`, `DEV-SDA-08`, `DEV-SRV-03`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's documentation updates log calls the July 2026 sale price change a clarification: a new Sale duration section of the merchant listing guide explains validFrom with validThrough or priceValidUntil, aligned with Merchant Center's sale_price_effective_date attribute.
  <br><sub>`D2-C507` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · is the documentation · [Latest documentation updates](https://developers.google.com/search/updates), [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing) · Used by `DEV-SDA-08`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's merchant listing guide says Product rich results only support pages that focus on a single product, or on several variants of the same product.
  <br><sub>`D2-C834` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · is the documentation · [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing) · Used by `DEV-SDA-07`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's merchant listing guide warns that a listing may not display if its priceValidUntil property indicates a past date.
  <br><sub>`D2-C835` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · is the documentation · [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing) · Used by `DEV-SDA-08`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Product structured data introduction says that providing both on-page structured data and a Merchant Center feed maximizes eligibility for shopping experiences and helps Google understand and verify the data; product snippets may take pricing from the feed when the markup lacks it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C344` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product) · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Merchant Center help says products and details crawled from an online store can show up on Google even when they are not marked up with schema.org or added in Merchant Center, and lists the Shopping tab among the places Merchant Center free listings appear.
  <br><sub>`D3-C347` · Google Merchant Center Help · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Free listings for products](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9199328?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Merchant Center's automatic item updates use structured data and other product data found on landing pages to fix price, sale price, availability and condition mismatches in a merchant's product data; Google says they do not replace regular feed updates.
  <br><sub>`D3-C350` · Google Merchant Center Help · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Allow Merchant Center to update product information automatically](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's merchant listing documentation recommends defining shipping and return policies once under Organization markup and referencing them from an Offer, even on another page, using only the @id keyword (through hasShippingService for shipping, hasMerchantReturnPolicy for returns).
  <br><sub>`D3-C384` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links · is the documentation · [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing) · Used by `DEV-SDA-09`</sub>

## Analysis

- **[Analysis]** On product pages with related-product or recently-viewed carousels, make sure the Product markup describes only the main item and its price; Google's own example of what markup prevents was pulling a price from related products.
  <br><sub>`D2-C475` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · Used by `DEV-SDA-07`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For time-limited sales, give the sale price its validity dates in the product markup (Google's merchant listing documentation describes validFrom, validThrough and priceValidUntil) instead of editing markup by hand when the sale ends, and keep the dates aligned with the Merchant Center feed.
  <br><sub>`D2-C508` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing), [Latest documentation updates](https://developers.google.com/search/updates) · Used by `DEV-SDA-08`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's free listings help says crawled store products can appear on Google without markup or Merchant Center but does not say whether that includes the Shopping tab; for a shop that wants Shopping tab visibility, the stage rule that Merchant Center is required is the safe working assumption.
  <br><sub>`D3-C348` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · [Free listings for products](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9199328?hl=en), [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For an online shop, Product structured data is enough for product rich results and Google Images product annotations, but the Shopping tab needs a Merchant Center feed too; keep feed and markup values identical, since Google can use the markup to validate the feed.
  <br><sub>`D3-C351` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** As of 3 October 2026 Google's Merchant Center help lists no schema.org property for question_and_answer, document_link, related_product, popularity_rank, variant_option or product_detail (only item_group_title maps, to ProductGroup.name), and Search Central does not document such markup: reading these attributes from schema.org is a stage statement, the feed is the documented route.
  <br><sub>`D3-C381` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links · [Question and answer [question_and_answer]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085211?hl=en), [Document link [document_link]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17084656?hl=en), [Related product [related_product]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085213?hl=en), [Popularity rank [popularity_rank]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085297?hl=en), [Variant option [variant_option]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085214?hl=en), [Product detail [product_detail]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9218260?hl=en), [Item group title [item_group_title]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085146?hl=en), [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing) · Used by `DEV-SHP-04`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Schema.org's release notes show version 30.1 (16 September 2026) added specification, isOftenBoughtWith and consumerNotice for Product, valueGroup for PropertyValue and itemPopularity for Offer as vocabulary for retail feed data; Google's Search Central docs did not yet document these properties on 3 October 2026.
  <br><sub>`D3-C400` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links · Used by `DEV-SHP-04`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Shop developers should first keep core feed and markup values (price, availability, brand, GTIN) accurate, then add Q&As, product highlights, specs as key-value product details and related products in the Merchant Center feed, and mirror them in schema.org Product markup only as Google documents support for it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C410` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links</sub>

## Built on these claims

The items of the developer and content kits that rest on this topic's claims.

- Requirement `DEV-ERR-04`: Keep temporarily out-of-stock product pages live with 200 and their current availability
- Requirement `DEV-SDA-07`: Describe only the page's main product in Product markup, not related-product carousels
- Requirement `DEV-SDA-08`: Mark up merchant listings completely, with validity dates for sale prices
- Requirement `DEV-SDA-09`: Declare return, shipping and loyalty policies once at organisation level
- Requirement `DEV-SHP-01`: Use Product markup for rich results and a Merchant Center feed for the Shopping tab, with identical values
- Requirement `DEV-SHP-04`: Treat product Q&A and specification markup in schema.org as an extra on top of the feed
- Requirement `DEV-SRV-03`: Answer planned maintenance and short outages with 503, for a day or two at most
- Glossary term *Merchant Center*
